title: Q4 Engineering Velocity & People Investment Huddle
summary: Leadership reviewed Q4 hiring commitments, infra velocity targets, on-call burdens, and a short roadmap of reliability investments. People team outlined hiring cadence and comp timing; engineering leadership presented targeted latency SLOs and Dedicated rollout milestones. Session ended with Q&A and a concrete set of follow-ups for hiring and a benchmark run.

Infra: run cross-region latency benchmark and share spreadsheet by 2025-11-25
Eng leads: finalize canary plan for Dedicated v1 by 2025-11-28
All: survey on on-call load to be sent Monday

Lena: schedule cross-region latency benchmark, share raw results (due 2025-11-25)
Derrick: draft canary rollback and monitoring playbook for Dedicated rollout (due 2025-11-28)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 01:12
Attendees: Maya Thompson, Priyanka Rao, Derrick Alvarez, Jules Kim, Sam Ortiz, Lena Wu, Arjun Singh, Nora Patel + all staff (listening)

Summary (auto): Leadership highlights hiring and infra reliability commitments for Q4, asks infra to run benchmarks, people to publish hiring tracker, and asks teams to reduce on-call toil via automation.

[00:00] Maya: Okay, hi everybody, uh thanks for joining — gonna kick off the huddle, thanks for being on time. We wanted to do a short, tight update on two big buckets: hiring/people, and engineering velocity / reliability. We'll keep this to about an hour, um ish.

[00:18] Jules: Quick context from People — we've bumped Q4 hiring to 18 new ICs and three managers, that's net of attrition; we are prioritizing infra, model infra, and two senior reliability SDEs. Nora and team will open panel interviews this week.

[00:36] Nora: Yep. We're running a small recruiter blitz — senior infra and quant infra. We have three green candidates in pipeline, two are onsite next week. There might be some scheduling wobble with holidays so heads-up.

[01:05] Priyanka: From the tech side, thanks. We have three engineering asks: one, reduce p95 for generation endpoints by 30% in 60 days; two, complete Dedicated v1 canary and rollback docs; three, reduce tail-memory spikes on long context requests. The first is about routing + batching config, we have some ideas.

[01:30] Derrick: On p95 target — I want to be explicit: this is per-route, not blanket. We need per-route SLOs in the console; Sam can speak to product. The trick will be balancing batching for cost vs latency for high-qps routes.

[01:50] Sam: Right. We'll map top-20 routes by cost and latency and propose per-route SLOs. We'll push a draft to the docs repo and notify the AEs.

[02:12] Lena: Benchmarks — infra will run a cross-region latency matrix: US-west, US-east, eu-west — with both hosted and dedicated stacks. We'll surface p50/p95/p99 numbers plus error-rate for 2k concurrent streams. We'll also test a KV-cache warm path vs cold. 

[02:40] Arjun: Quick note — the runtime team discovered a kernel-selection regression in the latest build; it causes a 7-12% degradation on long-context models when quantized. We're rolling back that patch and working to land a fix.

[03:05] Maya: Thanks. That regression note is useful — please treat as Sev-low until fixed but escalate if it affects benchmarks.

[03:22] Jules: People update — comp cycle: we will share the comp band adjustments internally next week. Managers should expect calibration sessions mid-December. Also, mental-health week in January is still on.

[03:40] Audience: (question) will the comp changes be retroactive?

[03:48] Jules: Short answer, no, not retroactive — adjustments apply to next cycle; exceptions for promotions will be handled case-by-case.

[04:05] Maya: On on-call — we heard you. We want to reduce single-person on-call ownership and increase runbooks + playbooks. Derrick, can you speak to rotations?

[04:18] Derrick: Yes, we plan to move to 2-person primary/secondary on-call for infra teams, shorten rotation lengths from 6 to 4 weeks for those with heavy incident load, and hire a dedicated reliability lead to shepherd runbooks. We also will build a self-service onboarding page for on-call.

[04:43] Arjun: Implementation detail — we'll extend the autoscaling buffer for steady-state to take pressure off on-call during traffic spikes; that's a config change in the serving layer. Could introduce small cost uptick.

[05:02] Maya: Cost vs latency trade-off again. We need transparency: show cost delta for the auto-buffer; product and finance to approve.

[05:14] Sam: We'll model three scenarios and share a matrix in the doc.

[05:30] [TIMESTAMP SKIP — jump to mid-point highlights]

[33:12] Priyanka: Question on Dedicated rollout — current status: staging canary is green, but we still need the canary rollback + health-check hooks. The team is blocked on a cross-region traffic-swap automation that Sam's team is helping with. We need that for a safe canary.

[33:35] Sam: We're pairing with infra to finish the traffic-swap automation. ETA end of week. Test plan will be in the ops repo.

[34:00] Lena: Bench results: initial staging numbers show p95 +10% worse than hosted because the dedup compression path isn't warmed. We'll re-run with KV-cache warm and we expect numbers to improve.

[34:22] Audience (chat comment): are there plans for private/on-prem customers for Q1?

[34:28] Maya: Yes, Private options are still in the roadmap for regulated customers; next year's cadence. Focus right now is reliability and Dedicated capacity for existing enterprise demand.

[35:05] [Short break — internal shoutouts]

[40:30] Jules: Shoutouts — recruiting closed two tough reqs, infra shipped the dynamic batching improvement, and the SRE team stabilized the mem-leak in the redis connector. Thanks team.

[41:05] Audience question from Slack: what does "reduce p95 by 30%" mean for product teams?

[41:18] Sam: Practically: target routes that are in the top 20 by token cost and have p95 above x ms. We'll propose route-level SLOs and a staging rollout.

[41:40] Maya: Also want to emphasize we need to avoid hero-oncall syndrome. If you see someone constantly paged, escalate to manager.

[42:00] Q&A session — clustered questions about hiring priorities and whether IC roles will be individual contributor heavy or team-lead heavy.

[46:30] Jules: We're prioritizing senior ICs for infra and ops automation, and two people managers for growth squads. We'll add those labels to the hiring tracker.

[47:10] Nora: For interview loops, we're introducing a standardized infra take-home for senior candidates to speed assessment.

[48:00] Arjun: Dev note — for the kernel regression we will revert the patch in canary today; we think that will recover the long-context perf numbers. Regression caused an ordering change in the matmul kernel selection, weird edge-case.

[48:28] Priyanka: Good. Also — please ensure any perf-change PR includes a small perf-harness run in CI. We should gate large perf-impact changes.

[49:02] Audience (mute-unmute): Will this slow down other work?

[49:08] Derrick: Short term yes, some feature work shifts to reliability and perf investigations. Long term we expect a net gain.

[49:25] Maya: Ok, near the end — let's recap next steps: Jules publishes hiring tracker, Lena shares full benchmark by Tues, Derrick posts canary runbook, Priyanka syncs with product prioritization.

[49:46] Maya: Questions after the meeting — please open a thread in #all-hands-questions or book time with your manager.

[50:05] Final quick pulse: How's everyone feeling about the plan? (emoji reaction pause)

[50:30] Maya: Thanks all. We'll keep these short moving forward.

[51:00] End of recording.

Notes/Artifacts referenced: hiring-tracker-link (internal doc), cross-region-latency-spreadsheet (to be uploaded), dedicated-canary-playbook (ops repo link).
